seo_title: SEBI Extends FPI KYC Review Cycle to 2 or 8 Years
title: SEBI Rationalises the KYC Review Cycle for Foreign Portfolio Investors to Two or Eight Years
court: Securities and Exchange Board of India
case_name: SEBI circular rationalising the periodic KYC review cycle for foreign portfolio investors
card_summary: SEBI has rationalised how often foreign portfolio investors must undergo KYC review, moving from the earlier one-year or three-year cycle to a new cycle of two years or eight years based on an FPI's category, jurisdiction and regulatory status. Government-securities-only FPIs and the SWAGAT-FI route keep their existing cycles. The change amends the 30 May 2024 master circular and takes effect from 1 December 2026.
card_tip: An FPI and its custodian should confirm which review cycle, two years or eight, now applies to its category before 1 December 2026 so a KYC lapse does not interrupt its registration.
verification_notes: The circular number, the 30 October 2026 date, the move to a two-year/eight-year cycle, the carve-outs for government-securities-only FPIs and SWAGAT-FI, and the 1 December 2026 effective date are confirmed against the SEBI circular itself and against Khaitan & Co's and Kotak Securities' notes, with Taxguru's report agreeing on the same points. The full category-by-jurisdiction table mapping which FPIs fall into the two-year versus eight-year cycle was not fully available in the sources checked and is not restated here. This item serves the foreign investor/foreign company audience named in the firm's current research priorities.
